_: Timing targets. Ratios, not absolute times, so they are speaking-rate independent.
_source: Each carries where the number comes from. A target with no source is a guess and should say so.

timing.what: a vowel is longer before a voiced consonant than a voiceless one
timing.source: House & Fairbanks 1953; Peterson & Lehiste 1960 put it near 1.5 for English
timing.note: one word, two vowels, different codas — across two words it is unreachable

timing.what: an open vowel is longer than a close one, all else equal
timing.note: open vowel then close vowel, same word

timing.what: a stressed syllable is longer than an unstressed one
timing.source: Klatt 1976; the unstressed-to-stressed range is wide across studies
timing.note: stress on the SECOND syllable, which is where banana has it

timing.what: the last syllable of an utterance is longer
timing.note: the last held vowel against the first, inside one word

timing.what: syllables get shorter as a word gets longer
timing.note: across two words of different length — unreachable until 8.1b makes D a rate

timing.what: a voiceless stop is held longer than a voiced one
